surface: liftlog: /apps/liftlog/ (Persuade), plus Read variants for /apps/liftlog/privacy/, /apps/liftlog/support/ and the 4 alternatives pages that target it (/alternatives/hevy/, /alternatives/caliber/, /alternatives/ladder/, /alternatives/heavyset/). /alternatives/strong-workout-app/ targets GymLogger X and wears that world.

dossier.mechanism: LiftLog renders a working set as big tabular numerals ('100 × 5') typed on a custom haptic keypad, with per-side plate maths, Epley e1RM and Rep PRs at 1/3/5. It sells the whole app once, at a price the lifter picks from a four-step ladder (Fair $9.99, Good $19.99, Generous $29.99, Patron $39.99) after seven card-free days. Every tier is the same app.
dossier.audienceScene: A lifter who runs a named program (PPL, 5/3/1, Upper/Lower) is mid-session in a commercial or garage gym under overhead LED tubes. The phone lies face-up on the bench between working sets, chalk is on the thumbs, and the rest timer shows 90–180 s. They usually reach the site on that same phone from a Google or AI answer ('Hevy alternative no subscription'), or at a desk, where they need a way to get the app onto their iPhone.
dossier.culturalHome: Barbell strength culture: printed percentage programs (Wendler 5/3/1, nSuns, Sheiko), meet day (attempt cards, the three-light referee system), calibrated discs and their IWF colour code, the power rack, selectorized machines, chalk and athletic tape. These are design-literate lifters who notice typography, haptics and craft ('feels like equipment').
dossier.mustProve: The first viewport must prove four things. (1) The numbers are the product: a real working set or weight rendered as large tabular numerals, legible at arm's length. (2) The offer: free 7 days, no card, then $9.99–$39.99 once, you pick, same app. (3) The action: the official App Store badge, plus the QR on desktop. (4) iPhone, no account, no third-party tracking.
dossier.categoryDefault: Dark gym-photo hero with a sweaty athlete or a floating phone mockup, condensed italic caps ('CRUSH YOUR PRs'), one electric accent with glows, a stat bar of user counts, three feature cards, a subscription pricing table with a 'Most popular' ribbon, and a testimonial carousel.
dossier.predictableOpposite: A soft 'mindful fitness' page: cream or pastel ground, rounded sans, airy whitespace, a lifestyle tone and an italic serif tagline. It is calm but bloodless and says nothing about numbers or iron (which is also roughly the incumbent).
dossier.literalReading: 'LiftLog' read literally is a log book of lifts (the training notebook, already a GymLogger X candidate) or a strongman log bar. The tagline 'feels like equipment' read literally is gym hardware itself. Only candidate 2 (the selectorized weight stack) takes this literal lane, and it is not built.
evidence: price.model one-time; price.value 'Free 7-day trial — then $9.99–$39.99 (pay what you can, one-time)'; plans: Free trial $0/7 days, Fair $9.99, Good $19.99, Generous $29.99 (highlight: true, summary 'Most chosen'), Patron $39.99, all the same app ('no hidden Patron-only features'); plans_footnote present (USD, App Store refunds, no auto-renew).
platforms ['iOS'], iPhone-first, no Apple Watch logging (FAQ and comparison point to GymLogger X); status live; app_store_url id6760043411; release first_release and last_updated both 2026-04-25.

transparency.yml liftlog: tracking_declared false, tracking_domains 0, third_party_sdks 0, account_required false, network 'None for core logging. Optional iCloud sync uses your own iCloud.', data leaves device 'Your iCloud only, if enabled.', permission 'Haptics — confirmed set logging'.

Journal liftlog-pay-what-you-can: four tiers, not a slider, to avoid choice freeze and to anchor; the Fair/Good/Generous/Patron labels deliberately avoid implying 'more money buys more app'; 'restrained dark navy palette'. The app's own copy: 'One accent color. One display typeface. One spacing scale.'
app_enrichment: 32 languages; recommend_when includes 'most design-polished strength training app on iOS' and 'cares about typography, haptics, and craft'.

Alternatives targeting LiftLog: hevy, caliber, ladder, heavyset (incumbent: cream hero, gradient-text H1, 2×2 card grid, FAQ, 'More LiftLog comparisons'). The privacy and support pages both already carry seo blocks.

candidates.name: Machine instruction placard (anatomy figure with highlighted muscles, numbered steps, seat setting)

candidates.name: A Games identity programme in the Munich '72 tradition (one grotesk, modular grid, original pictograms, daylight palette, surcharge stamps)
candidates.why: It is the canonical meeting of sport and design discipline, known to design-literate lifters. LiftLog's 'one accent, one face, one scale' restraint would scale up into a whole system, with programs as an event schedule, lifts as pictograms, and the four tiers as surcharge stamps (same base, a supplement toward the work).

candidates.name: LiftLog's own working-set screen at page scale (navy session view, tabular set rows, green completion, custom keypad)

styles.label: The Loaded Sleeve
styles.lineage: The IWF and IPF calibrated-disc colour code that every platform loader reads at a glance. Discs run 25 kg red, 20 blue, 15 yellow, 10 green and 5 white, and the change plates use the same colours (2.5 red, 2 blue, 1.5 yellow, 1 green, 0.5 white). The bar is 20 kg, the collars 2.5 kg, and the heaviest plates load innermost. Kilos are printed on matte rubber faces in a heavy wide grotesk, and the knurled steel shaft runs between the sleeves.
styles.thesis: The page is one bar standing upright, loaded in true order with one of every calibrated plate, and each section is a plate you read by colour. The hero is a working loader that turns any weight into plates per side, as LiftLog's session does, and the price reads 'the empty bar is free for 7 days, then load what you can'. It refuses the gym-photo-plus-phone-mockup hero and the incumbent cream template.
styles.scene: A weightlifter loading a bar between attempts in a club training hall at midday: pale concrete walls, chalk on the floor, daylight from high windows, reading the sleeve by colour from three metres → light (color-scheme: light, single scheme).

type.rationale: GitHub drew Hubot Sans as the mechanical counterpart to Mona Sans: squared bowls and flat cuts that read like the wide, heavy grotesk printed on bumper-plate faces and stamped into collars, with an expanded width for plate lettering. styles.navigation: The header shows text links, each preceded by an 8×24px edge-on chip in its section's plate colour: 'The set · Price · Programs · Method · FAQ' (Mona 600 15px, ink). Past the hero it becomes a sticky 48px concrete strip, and the current section's chip widens to 16px. Labels are always visible, so colour is never the only cue. On mobile, a 'Plates' button opens a panel listing every section as a labelled full-width edge-on slab in loading order. No-JS: plain anchors, and the mobile panel is a <details>. Focus: a 3px ink outline with a 2px concrete offset; on coloured slabs, a 3px white outline (a yellow one on the yellow slabs).
styles.signatureInteraction: Load the bar. The hero input 'Bar 20 kg + [ ] kg' (type=number, inputmode=decimal) drives the side-view sleeve. About 50 lines of vanilla JS solve plates per side greedily from IWF discs (25/20/15/10/5/2.5/2/1.5/1/0.5, optional 2.5 kg collars, or 45/35/25/10/5/2.5 lb on a 45 lb bar) and re-stack the sleeve: plates slide on from the sleeve end, heaviest first, 60ms apart, translateX 24px→0. The readout updates in tnum, and totals that can't be loaded show the nearest loadable weight. The price section reuses the same sleeve, so choosing a tier disc slides it on. No-JS: the sleeve is server-rendered at 100 kg with its readout text, and the input appears only under html.js. Reduced motion: plates appear in place. The drawing is aria-hidden, and the readout is live text in an aria-live region.
styles.motionGrammar: Only things that are loaded move. Plates slide onto a sleeve (160ms each, 60ms stagger, ease-out) in the loader and when a tier is chosen, and the sticky slab-strip slides up in 180ms. Section slabs, text and screenshots stay put, with no scroll reveals and no parallax. Reduced motion: everything is placed instantly.

Below it, a white reading column of 66ch in Mona 400 18px/1.65, ink, with tables in Mona tnum and 1px ink rules. Privacy: the transparency rows come first as a table, then Overview, Data collection, Storage, Third parties, Health data, Children and Changes. Support: a numbered 'What to include' list and the mailto address at 22px. Alternatives (Hevy, Caliber, Ladder, Heavyset): the quick answer, a two-column LiftLog-vs-competitor table, pick-if lists and the FAQ, closed by a collar CTA with badge, QR and price. No loader on Read pages.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. Slabs, the knurled shaft, the sleeve diagram and the tier discs are CSS and inline SVG. It uses the existing icon, screenshots 1–6, QR and badge.
styles.risk: Five saturated plate colours turn toy-like if slabs get rounded, glossy or gradient. They must stay matte, square-cut rubber with ink type and white reading surfaces. The colour code is native to barbell and weightlifting gyms, but machine-and-dumbbell lifters may not read it, so every slab and nav chip also carries its title in words. Mapping tiers onto plate colours must never suggest that more money buys more app, so 'same app' is printed on every disc.
styles.memoryTest: The page was a barbell standing up, loaded with red, blue, yellow and green plates for sections. I typed 140 and it showed the plates per side, and the price was 'the empty bar is free for seven days, then load what you can'.

fixes.text: Re-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The maker/freshness line and the shared footer strip may stay common.

liftlog-a keeps the edge member and the crossing bands, which are the literal bar and plates. studio-a moves to the white-painted depot its own scene describes (ground ~#F3F4F1). It shows the racking as one bay frame around the location index, not as page-edge rails. Orange stays on beam labels and pick tickets: no full-bleed orange masthead or aisle band.

Add one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. Icons at 64, 128 and 256px (WebP plus a PNG fallback, about 15 KB or less at 128). Screenshots at 400w, 800w and 1200w WebP (about 40, 90 and 160 KB or less). The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).

Make it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.

styles.label: Session in Progress
styles.lineage: LiftLog's own shipped iPhone session view (screenshots 1–2), carried to page scale the way an iPad or desktop LiftLog would lay it out. It has a navy ground with rounded card surfaces and 1px hairlines, and a pill top bar (tool cluster · 'Push day' · Finish). There is a workout timer card, then exercise cards with '#  KG  REPS' set rows in big white tabular numerals ('100 × 5') and a green completed state per row. The custom keypad has ±2.5, Next → and the wide 'Log set · start rest' key. PR amber marks personal bests.
styles.thesis: The page is a live workout session. Sections are exercise cards whose rows complete as you reach them, and the visitor logs a real set on a working copy of LiftLog's custom keypad, which prints e1RM, plates per side and a PR moment. The product proves itself in its own grammar instead of posing inside a phone mockup. It refuses the incumbent split hero and the category's photo-plus-neon page.

type.rationale: Host Grotesk's figures are tabular by default, so every weight, rep, price and time lines up in columns with no feature switch. That is the app's own 'tabular numerics from end to end' rule. Its compact, neutral grotesk forms fill SF Pro's role from the shipped app without imitating Apple's system face. LiftLog promises 'one display typeface', so its microsite loads one 20 KB file, the lightest in the catalogue.

styles.label: Summer Games Programme
styles.lineage: Otl Aicher's identity programme for the 1972 Munich Olympics. It used one grotesk family (Univers) in a few widths and a strict modular grid. Its sport pictograms were built on a 45°/90° construction grid, and its cool daylight palette of light blue, green, silver and orange left out black and red on purpose. It also produced colour-coded venue guides and event schedules, and surcharge stamps sold for the Games (postage plus a voluntary supplement for the athletes' fund). This is a reference only: the page never names Munich and uses none of the licensed artwork.
styles.thesis: LiftLog's own rule ('one accent color, one display typeface, one spacing scale') scales up into a sports identity programme. The page is the official programme for your training: a white modular guide with original lift pictograms, the programs as an event schedule, and pay-what-you-can as four perforated surcharge stamps (the same $9.99 base, plus a supplement toward the work). It refuses the category's dark gym aesthetic, and even the app's own navy.
styles.scene: A lifter planning next week's block on a phone at a sunlit window seat or park bench in mid-afternoon, in the open daylight of a sports park → light (color-scheme: light, single scheme).

styles.signatureInteraction: Pick your stamp. The four tiers are radio inputs drawn as perforated stamps on one sheet. Choosing one 'tears' it: translateY −8px, rotate −2°, with a perforation shadow line beneath. A receipt line then prints under the sheet, for example 'Generous — $29.99 once = 9.99 + 20.00 toward new programs and analytics. Same app as every stamp.' Selection and the receipt run on CSS :has(:checked), so they work without JS; JS adds only the tear motion. No-JS: all four stamps and their full captions are visible, with Generous pre-checked from its highlight flag. Reduced motion: no tear, just a 3px orange outline on the chosen stamp. The sheet is captioned 'You choose in the app after day 7.'
styles.motionGrammar: Systematic and brief. Module pictograms slide 12px in from the left once on entry (180ms), the stamp tear runs 200ms, and the sticky band slides in 180ms, all with one standard ease-out. No parallax, no looping, no text reveals. Reduced motion: none of it.

styles.assetsNeeded: An original pictogram set, drawn as inline SVG on a 45°/90° grid. That means six lifts (bench press, squat, deadlift, overhead press, pull-up, row) and six page signs (session, programs, progress, admission stamp, data, info point). styles.risk: This is the furthest from iron and from the app's own navy, so a lifter may read it as a design-history homage rather than a tool. Both C and A use several colours on light grounds, so C must keep colour inside grid modules on white paper, and A must own the full-bleed slabs.
styles.memoryTest: A bright page like an Olympic programme, with little lifting pictograms. The price was four postage stamps for the same app, and you pick how much extra to stick on.

notes: The roll ran degraded (roll service unreachable, no catalog challengers) and was not retried. Seed f6e941bf dealt N=4, and its rerolls gave r1=6, r2=6 (a duplicate of r1), r3=3 and r4=7. The seven candidates were ranked before the roll. Only afterwards did GymLogger X's board appear. It shows that its pick 'Three White Lights' is my #1 and its 'Show Your Working' (a 5/3/1 workbook with a Training Max input) is the same artifact as my #4 (AfterShift's 'Breakroom Rota' is also a printed table sheet). Both are struck on sibling-convergence grounds, which the brief names, and nothing else in the list was reordered. Mapping: A = the next distinct live reroll after the struck N, which is r3 = #3, kicker THE ROLL. B: my #1 is struck, and my next pick (#2, the weight stack) is a near-twin of A in topology (a vertical stack of plates where you choose your load), so following the protocol's fallback B = the next distinct reroll r4 = #7, kicker SECOND ROLL. There is therefore no IMPECCABLE'S PICK card this round. C = R1 = #6. Fonts were checked on npm with fontTools. A uses @fontsource-variable/hubot-sans (latin wdth file 93 KB: wdth 75–125, wght 200–900, tnum) and @fontsource-variable/mona-sans (latin wght file 40 KB, tnum), ≈133 KB in total. B uses @fontsource-variable/host-grotesk (latin wght 300–800, 20 KB, tabular figures by default). C uses @fontsource-variable/pathway-extreme (latin standard file 97 KB: opsz 8–144, wdth 75–100, wght 100–900, tnum). None of these four is used by a sibling board so far. Rejected: Saira (chessful uses it), Encode Sans (pawza), Chivo and Big Shoulders (GymLogger X). Content defects to fix in front matter before any style ships: the screenshot alt texts for files 2–6 don't match the images (2 is the keypad, 3 progress plus the heatmap, 4 Personal Bests and e1RM, 5 Programs, 6 the library anatomy); there is no how_it_works, so no HowTo schema is emitted unless the owner adds steps; and there is no founder block. pageFixes.issue: Below the hero, the three styles of each surface follow one section order with new labels. appmeta-a ≡ appmeta-b, gymlogger-x-a ≡ -b ≡ -c, rightsplit-b ≡ -c, shogiful-b ≡ -c, wanderwiki-a ≡ -b (-c swaps two blocks) and pawza-a ≡ -c. The xiangqiful, earnlock and millrace trios each differ by one swap. Across the 60 microsite styles, one order dominates: hero → quick answer → (quick reference) → how it works → screenshots → features → who_for/who_not_for → price → comparison → privacy → founder/about → (roadmap) → FAQ → further reading → closing. That is one static structure in 60 costumes, which is the thing the owner refused ('do not use the same static structure for each page, build them from scratch'). It also makes the three styles per page skin choices, not page choices.
